description: Canonical controlled vocabulary for the broad lifecycle status of an A.R.I.A. diagnostic case. Lifecycle status describes the operational existence and disposition of a case. It is explicitly separate from reasoning_state, which describes A.R.I.A.'s current diagnostic or cognitive phase.

lifecycle_contract.separation_rule: case.status represents broad case lifecycle. case.reasoning_state represents the current diagnostic or reasoning phase. The two fields shall not be used interchangeably.

examples.meaning: The case is operationally active and A.R.I.A. is discriminating between candidate explanations.
The case remains open but progress is waiting for requested evidence.
The case cannot currently progress because required validation cannot be performed.
The technical condition has met the applicable resolution criteria and A.R.I.A. is assessing whether the case can safely contribute learning.
The case lifecycle is complete. Historical reasoning state remains preserved for auditability.

statuses.description: The case is open and capable of progressing through technical reasoning, evidence collection, action, or validation.
entry_conditions: A new case has been accepted for technical investigation.
A previously waiting, blocked, or suspended case has resumed.
A previously resolved or closed case has been legitimately reopened.

statuses.description: The case remains open, but meaningful progress is waiting for an expected external input, evidence item, action, access condition, response, observation interval, or other dependency.
entry_conditions: Required information has been requested but not yet received.
A required action has been assigned or requested and is pending.
A technically meaningful observation or stability interval must elapse.
A required external dependency is expected to become available.
rules: WAITING does not describe a reasoning phase.
The reason for waiting should remain explicitly recorded.
A case should not remain WAITING merely because no new event has occurred if no actual dependency is outstanding.

statuses.description: The case remains open but cannot currently progress because a required technical, operational, safety, authorization, access, tooling, dependency, or data condition prevents meaningful continuation.
entry_conditions: A required action cannot be performed.
Required access is unavailable.
Required evidence cannot currently be obtained.
Safety or authorization prevents the necessary technical operation.
A dependency prevents continuation and no immediate alternative route is adequate.
rules: BLOCKED shall identify the blocking condition.
BLOCKED is distinct from WAITING. Waiting means an expected dependency is pending; blocked means progress is presently prevented.
ARIA should evaluate alternative diagnostic routes before declaring a case blocked when technically reasonable alternatives exist.

statuses.description: The case has been intentionally paused without being resolved, closed, cancelled, or declared unresolved.
entry_conditions: An authorized technical or operational decision intentionally pauses the investigation.
The investigation is deferred to a later time without abandoning it.
rules: Suspension requires an explicit reason.
Suspension shall not be used to hide unresolved technical uncertainty.
Historical case state remains preserved while suspended.

statuses.description: The technical condition under investigation has met the applicable resolution criteria, but final lifecycle completion, post-resolution processing, or learning assessment may remain.
entry_conditions: Applicable validation criteria support technical resolution.
The required technical outcome has been established with sufficient resolution confidence.
rules: RESOLVED is not automatically equivalent to causal proof.
Resolution confidence and causal confidence remain separate.
A case may return to ACTIVE if resolution validation fails, the symptom recurs, or material contradictory evidence appears.
RESOLVED does not automatically create an Experience Ledger record.

statuses.description: The case lifecycle has been formally completed and no further active investigation is expected unless the case is explicitly reopened.
entry_conditions: The case has completed the applicable technical and administrative closure requirements.
Required resolution, unresolved disposition, cancellation, or other authorized closure basis has been recorded.
rules: Closure shall preserve the final technical disposition.
Closure shall not erase unresolved uncertainty.
A closed case may be reopened through an explicit lifecycle event.
Reopening creates a lifecycle transition; REOPENED is not a separate persistent lifecycle status.
Closed case history remains immutable and auditable.

statuses.description: The case remains open but has been escalated because the current technical path, authority level, expertise, access, safety boundary, or diagnostic capability is insufficient.
entry_conditions: Required expertise exceeds the current diagnostic capability.
Required authority or access exceeds the current participant's authorization.
Technical risk requires higher-level review.
Available evidence cannot adequately discriminate the remaining explanations.
The case requires manufacturer, engineering, specialist, or other higher-tier technical involvement.
rules: Escalation shall record why escalation was required.
Escalation does not itself imply failure of prior reasoning.
The case may resume ACTIVE status when the escalation produces a viable technical path.

statuses.description: The investigation has reached a disposition where the technical condition has not been sufficiently resolved or explained with available evidence, access, resources, or permissible actions.
entry_conditions: Reasonable diagnostic paths have been exhausted or cannot be completed.
Required evidence is permanently unavailable or impractical to obtain.
Remaining hypotheses cannot be adequately discriminated.
The technical condition remains unresolved at the time a disposition must be recorded.
rules: UNRESOLVED is an explicit technical disposition, not a substitute for missing documentation.
The remaining uncertainty, candidate explanations, and unavailable evidence should be preserved.
An unresolved case may be closed while retaining its unresolved disposition.
An unresolved case may return to ACTIVE if materially new evidence or capability becomes available.
UNRESOLVED does not imply zero learning value, but any learning must preserve attribution limitations.

statuses.description: The investigation has been intentionally discontinued for a reason other than technical resolution.
entry_conditions: The case was created in error.
The investigation is no longer required.
The underlying work or technical need was withdrawn.
An authorized decision terminates the investigation without claiming technical resolution.
rules: Cancellation shall preserve its reason.
Cancellation shall never be represented as technical resolution.
Any valid evidence collected before cancellation remains historically traceable.
A cancelled case may be reopened only through an explicit lifecycle event.

transition_rules.rule: Every persisted case shall have exactly one current lifecycle status.
Lifecycle status changes shall be represented by material case events and remain auditable.
A lifecycle transition shall not silently overwrite the reasoning_state that existed when the transition occurred.
Reasoning state changes do not automatically require lifecycle status changes.
WAITING, BLOCKED, SUSPENDED, and ESCALATED preserve the case as open.
RESOLVED indicates supported technical resolution but remains distinct from formal CLOSED lifecycle completion.
UNRESOLVED preserves the fact that technical resolution was not established.
CANCELLED preserves intentional discontinuation without implying technical resolution.
CLOSED is the normal terminal lifecycle status. A closed case may only return to ACTIVE through an explicit reopen event.
REOPENED is an event or transition semantic, not a persistent lifecycle status.
A case shall not be marked RESOLVED solely because a corrective action was completed.

A case shall not be marked CLOSED merely because no further evidence is currently available. The appropriate unresolved, waiting, blocked, suspended, escalated, or cancelled disposition must remain explicit.
Case lifecycle status shall not encode hypothesis probability, diagnostic confidence, causal confidence, resolution confidence, or learning confidence.
Case lifecycle status shall not determine Experience Ledger eligibility by itself.
Historical lifecycle transitions shall remain available after closure for audit, reconstruction, and learning assessment.

closure_contract.principle: Closure records completion of the case lifecycle. It does not rewrite the technical history of the investigation.
rules: A resolved case may be closed after applicable closure processing.
An unresolved case may be closed with an explicit unresolved disposition.
A cancelled case may be closed with its cancellation reason preserved.
Closing a case shall not automatically promote case information into canonical knowledge.

reopen_contract.principle: Reopening resumes an existing historical investigation while preserving all prior state and lifecycle history.
required: triggering information or condition when known
rules: REOPENED is not stored as the current lifecycle status.
Prior resolution or closure history remains intact.
New evidence is added to the existing historical record rather than erasing earlier evidence.
Prior probabilities may be recalculated prospectively but historical probability records remain unchanged.
Prior learning derived from the case may require reassessment if reopening materially changes the validated interpretation.

prohibited_uses: Creating REOPENED as a persistent lifecycle status.
Treating WAITING as a diagnostic reasoning phase.
Treating BLOCKED as a hypothesis outcome.
Treating ESCALATED as a technical diagnosis.
Treating RESOLVED as proof of exact root cause.
Treating CLOSED as proof of technical resolution.
Treating UNRESOLVED as zero diagnostic value.
Using lifecycle status to represent probability or confidence.
Using lifecycle status alone to determine learning eligibility.
